previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a complex medical history including end-stage renal disease, pancreatic transplant, mechanical mitral valve, and heart failure was admitted for left leg cellulitis following a bug bite at her dialysis center. She presented with fever, chills, nausea, and worsening leg pain. She had been on reduced-dose warfarin, leading to an elevated INR of 4 on admission. She was treated with intravenous vancomycin after initial broad-spectrum antibiotics at an outside hospital. Her infection improved, INR normalized, and warfarin was safely restarted. She received one session of hemodialysis during admission and was transitioned back to her baseline medications, including metoprolol, which had been held. She was discharged home with a plan to complete a 10-day course of vancomycin via dialysis, monitor INR, and follow up with her care teams.
problems: Cellulitis and abscess of leg, except foot
Anticoagulants causing adverse effects in therapeutic use
Heart valve replaced by other means
Ulcer of other part of foot

Brief Hospital Course:
___ F with complicated PMHx including CAD s/p CABG, ESRD 
on HD ___, heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, s/p 
pancreatic and renal transplant, s/p recent hospitalization for 
cellulitis, who presented to hospital here with rapid A fib with 
RVR and repeat cellulitis

# Recurrent Nonpurulent cellulitis - Likely portal of entry of 
infection from new bug bite (patient had bite ___, developed 
cellulitis around posterior left thigh and was subsequently 
treated with vancomycin ___ successfully, got new bug 
bite ___ on lower left anterior leg, and developed cellulitis 
again). . High concern for MRSA given her recent 
hospitalizations. After initial doses of vancomycin resulted in 
remarkable improvement for cellulitis, it was determined 
patient's cellulitis was indeed a new infection ___ a bug bite 
and did not represent treatment failure of past cellulitis, and 
patient was put on vancomycin per HD protocol (after HD 
sessions) from ___. 

# Fever: Patient spiked isolated fever to 102 degrees on ___ 
pain culture workup was unrevealing (blood cx, CXR); and 
renal-transplant was consulted who suggested checking 
amylase/lipase and getting a pancreatic U/S (pancreatic U/S 
unremarkable, amylase/lipase slightly elevated above baseine at 
mid ___ but subsequently downtrended to 240/173). The pt 
continued to spike low grade fevers of 100.6 which correlated to 
after dialysis sessions.  Cultures were taken after each fever 
and all were finalized as no growth. Her HD line was never 
cultured and the pt was kept off antibiotics to maximize culture 
data. No source was identified, but there was concern for 
pancreatic rejection (see below). 

# Pancreatic Transplant Rejection: On ___ the pt had abdominal 
pain and a doubling of lipase and amylase. There was some 
concern for pancreatic rejection, however blood sugars remained 
normal. A CT of the pancreatic transplant did not reveal any 
signs of rejection or inflammation. Nevertheless, she was 
treated with an increased dose of prednisone 60mg PO which was 
taper to 40. She was discharged on 20mg with follow up in the 
transplant clinic. She remained on bactrim ppx. Her tracrolimus 
was increased from 2 to 2.5 q12 as her troughs were slightly 
low. 

#Coffee Ground Emesis: the pt had an episode of coffee ground 
emesis and a dropping Hb/Hct in the context of INR >5. She was 
typed and screened and transfused. An EGD revealed coffee ground 
emesis but no active source of bleeding. It was thought this 
bleeding was 2'/2 supratherapeutic INR. She was given vitamin K 
to bring down her INR. She had no further episodes of coffee 
ground emesis.

#Acute Blood Loss Anemia: The pt had slow bleeds with guaiac 
positive, melanotic stools. Her INR was supratherapeutic during 
these times. She required 1u pRBC transfusion approximately 
every other day. When her INR decreased to below 2, her stools 
became guiaic negative and her Hb/Hct stabilized. 

# Foot ulcer: Given concern for possible GNR/anaerobic cocurrent 
infection in context of patient's longstanding LLE ulcer on her 
foot, patient's podiatrist was contacted; who noted that 
patient's ulcer did not probe to bone and did not have concern 
for osteomyeltis. Xrays showed changes consistent with 
osteomyelitis. This was, however, thought to be related to the 
osteomyelitis she was treated for in ___. The skin overlying 
the ulcers was well granulated with out evidence of current 
infection. She was therefore not treated for osteomyelitis.  

# Rapid Afib w/RVR: Patient had found to be in paroxysmal afib 
RVR and elevated troponin in ED; but was evaluated by cardiology 
who felt that afib w/ RVR likely in setting of known CAD, 
elevated HR likely ___ catecholamine surge in setting of 
cellulitis, and felt no further management was needed save for 
continuing patine'ts home CAD meds and anticoagulation (for 
which patient is on for her mechanical MCR). Patient had 
elevated troponin as well following event (see below)

# Tropninemia: Rise in troponin from .49 ___pisode am

LEFT FOOT, THREE VIEWS:  

COMPARISON:  Left foot radiographs from ___.  

No localizing history available.  Allowing for this, there is soft tissue
swelling about the foot, with scattered dense vascular calcification. 
Compared with ___, there is new erosion at the base of the first
metatarsal.  Probable more subtle changes at the base of the second through
fifth metatarsals. In addition, the lateral view on today's exam shows slight
plantar angulation at the tarsometatarsal joints.  

Compared with the prior study, the distal phalanx of the third digit has been
removed.  The patient has also undergone apparent bunionectomy of the medial
aspect of the distal second metatarsal. In addition, there is new joint space
narrowing and cortical ill-definition of the first MTP joint.  

Incidental note is made of probable old healed fracture at the base of the
fifth metatarsal, unchanged compared with ___. Background osteopenia is
noted.

IMPRESSION:

1.  Correlation with specific site of ulceration is recommended for best
assessment.  

2.  New erosive change at the base of the first metatarsal and about the first
MTP joint, which raise concern for osteomyelitis.  Also probable changes at
multiple TMT joints and new slight plantar angulation in the mid foot.  These
latter findings could reflect either changes of Charcot arthropathy or
osteomyelitis and clinical correlation is requested for further assessment. 
If clinically indicated, MRI or bone scan/white blood cell scan could help for
further assessment. Please note that the initial resident wet reading did not
describe these findings. 

3.  Truncation of the medial aspect of the second metatarsal head nd absence
of much of the third distal phalanx appears to represent postoperative change.
Clinical correlation requested for further assessment.  

4.  Soft tissue swelling and vascular calcification.  No subcutaneous
emphysema identified. 

Submitted to critical results dashboard.

EXAMINATION:  CT ABD AND PELVIS W/O CONTRAST

INDICATION:  ___ woman with abdominal pain, drop in hematocrit and
elevated INR. Please evaluate for retroperitoneal hematoma.

TECHNIQUE:  Contiguous axial multidetector CT images through the abdomen and
pelvis without contrast.  Multiplanar reformations.

Total DLP: 342 mGy-cm

COMPARISON:  CT abdomen and pelvis from ___

FINDINGS: 

Lower chest: Limited view of lung bases is notable for diffuse areas of
ground-glass opacification and mild interlobular septal thickening, relatively
unchanged compared to the prior examination, probably reflecting mild
pulmonary edema.  A small left pleural effusion is also unchanged.  Moderate
cardiomegaly is stable.

CT abdomen: Evaluation of intra-abdominal organs is limited by lack of
intravenous contrast.  Noncontrast enhanced appearance of the liver,
gallbladder, spleen, and adrenal glands is unremarkable. The pancreas is not
well evaluated. Bilateral native kidneys are severely atrophic, unchanged.
Transplanted kidney in the right lower quadrant does not show hydronephrosis.

The stomach is partially expanded with ingested material some of which appear
hyperdense.  There is an anastomotic site in the left mid abdomen associated
with the pancreatic transplant.  The small bowel at the site is newly dilated
up to as much as 7.5 cm in diameter with hyperdense content.  Generally
shortly following the site, bowel caliber is normal but with some prominent
fluid content.  There is no highly discrete transition point but some degree
of obstruction is possible immediately beyond the anastomosis.  Stool and air
are present, and mildly prominent, through the colon, which is not dilated. 
Some colonic contents, particularly on the left, appear hyperdense measuring
approximately 58 Hounsfield units (2:57).

There is no intra-abdominal free air or fluid.  There is no lymphadenopathy. 
Severe diffuse atherosclerotic calcifications are present throughout the
arterial system.  The aorta is of normal caliber without aneurysmal
dilatation.

CT pelvis: The bladder is collapsed. There is no pelvic or inguinal
lymphadenopathy. There is no pelvic free fluid.

Bone windows: No suspicious lytic or sclerotic osseous lesion is identified.

IMPRESSION: 

1.  No evidence of retroperitoneal hematoma.

2.  Hyperdense contents within stomach and more distal bowel; this would
commonly be due to recent administration of hyperdense medication but blood
products within the lumen are a possible reason.

3.  Findings concerning for some degree of bowel obstruction, possibly
partial, along the distal side of anastomoses associated with the pancreatic
transplant.  An ileus would also be a differential diagnosis.  The dilated
loop is visible on the scout view and possibly amenable to follow-up using
radiography, although CT with enteric contrast and long preparation may be
helpful to evaluate further if the possibility of small bowel obstruction is a
clinical concern.

3.  Moderate cardiomegaly and mild pulmonary interstitial edema; extensive
vascular calcification.

Final report discussed with Dr. ___ on ___ by telephone.

Mottled appearance of the liver is demonstrated with patchy enhancement is

Subcentimeter anterior splenic hypodensity, too small to characterize,

Markedly atrophic bilateral calcified native kidneys.

Ingested material within the stomach. Stool is demonstrated throughout the
colon. Enteroenteric left lower quadrant anastomosis again seen. Mild

Patient is post pancreatic and renal transplant. 1 cm renal cyst. No

Severe calcification of abdominal aorta and branches. Mild retroperitoneal and

No suspicious osseous lesions. Dehiscence of the inferior sternum with
